question: What is the primary function of the jejunum in the gastrointestinal tract?

options.A: Storage of fecal waste before defecation

explanation: The jejunum contains large circular folds that maximize the surface area required for absorbing broken-down food particles. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T8#GNS213_U3_T8_h1)

question: How do microvilli contribute to the efficiency of the small intestine?

options.A: They secrete thick mucus to lubricate hard stool masses
options.B: They propel undigested food backward toward the stomach
options.C: They destroy pathogenic bacteria using strong digestive enzymes
options.D: They drastically expand the mucosal surface area for absorption

explanation: Tiny brush border projections create a massive absorptive surface that allows efficient transfer of nutrients into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T8#GNS213_U3_T8_h1)

question: Which change in the bowel wall is characteristic of Crohn's disease?

options.A: Inflammation of all layers with healthy patches in between
options.C: Shallow sores only in the rectum
options.D: Permanent widening of the large colon

explanation: Crohn's disease affects all layers of the intestinal wall and typically presents with alternating patches of diseased and healthy tissue. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T8#GNS213_U3_T8_h2)

question: Why is replacing fluids the immediate priority when a patient has a severe intestinal infection?

options.A: Water intake directly kills invading parasites in the gut
options.B: Pathogens consume all blood volume in the vessels
options.C: Damaged intestinal cells cause rapid loss of water and minerals
options.D: Hydration prevents the liver from producing toxic waste

explanation: Infection compromises the absorptive lining, leading to severe fluid depletion that must be corrected to prevent shock. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T8#GNS213_U3_T8_h2)

question: What is a very common cause of small bowel blockage in patients who have had prior surgeries?

options.A: Internal scar tissue from previous operations

explanation: Fibrous scar tissue from previous abdominal surgeries frequently binds loops of the small bowel together, causing mechanical blockage. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T8#GNS213_U3_T8_h3)

question: What kind of bowel sounds do you usually hear early on in a mechanical bowel obstruction?
explanation: The bowel works extra hard to push contents past a blockage, resulting in high-pitched, hyperactive sounds early in the obstruction. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T8#GNS213_U3_T8_h3)

question: What dietary protein triggers the immune response in celiac disease?
explanation: Gluten found in wheat, barley, and rye provokes an autoimmune reaction that flattens intestinal villi in celiac disease. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T8#GNS213_U3_T8_h4)

question: Why does removing a large part of the small intestine lead to severe nutritional problems?

options.A: The stomach stops producing enzymes for protein breakdown
options.B: Bile production by the liver immediately stops
options.C: The large intestine takes over and actively secretes vitamins
options.D: The remaining surface area is too small to absorb nutrients

explanation: Removing large sections of the small bowel drastically reduces the absorptive mucosal area, preventing adequate nutrient uptake. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T8#GNS213_U3_T8_h4)

question: Which procedure allows a doctor to look directly at the intestinal lining and take a tissue sample?
explanation: Endoscopy allows direct visualization of the intestinal lining and retrieval of tissue samples for laboratory confirmation. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T8#GNS213_U3_T8_h5)

question: What finding on an abdominal X-ray strongly suggests an intestinal blockage?

options.A: Multiple air and fluid levels within swollen bowel loops
options.B: Enlargement of the left kidney outline
options.D: Complete absence of any gas in the abdomen

explanation: Trapped gas and fluid pooling inside blocked intestinal segments create distinct air-fluid levels on upright x-rays. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T8#GNS213_U3_T8_h5)

question: What is the immediate goal when managing a patient with an acute bowel obstruction?

options.A: Give a high-fiber diet to stimulate movement
options.D: Rest the bowel and decompress the stomach using a tube

explanation: Keeping the patient fasting and using a nasogastric tube relieves pressure inside the bowel and prevents further distension. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T8#GNS213_U3_T8_h6)

question: When is surgery to remove part of the small intestine typically needed?

options.A: When stool consistency becomes slightly soft
options.B: As the very first step for any mild gut inflammation
options.C: When tissue damage, dead tissue, or a hole develops
options.D: To replace standard antibiotic therapy in infections

explanation: Physical damage like tissue death or structural blockage that threatens bowel integrity requires surgical removal. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T8#GNS213_U3_T8_h6)

question: Which vital sign changes are early warning signs of developing infection from a ruptured bowel?

options.A: High blood pressure and slow pulse
options.D: Slow heart rate and low body temperature

explanation: Infection and systemic inflammation typically trigger an elevated heart rate and elevated body temperature. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T8#GNS213_U3_T8_h7)

question: What is the most important diet change for a patient newly diagnosed with celiac disease?

options.A: Consume only liquids for the rest of your life
options.B: Avoid all foods containing wheat, barley, and rye
options.C: Increase intake of whole grain wheat for extra fiber
options.D: Avoid dairy products completely to prevent bloating

explanation: Strict avoidance of gluten grains is required to allow the small intestinal lining to heal and prevent symptoms from returning. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T8#GNS213_U3_T8_h7)
